quests.title: The Warm Range
quests.synopsis: A reading is a measurement. Follow the cable run east and find what the machines were built to serve.

stages.title: A Reading
stages.narrativePrompt: The geophone pit reads the valley like a slow heartbeat, and the cable runs east under the treeline. Somebody once knew where it went.

choices.text: Walk the cable run east to the fuse world and read the linen charters.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The linen codes decode to the Standard. The machine kept the codes after the staff stopped keeping the shifts. The swept path ends at a tape door.

choices.text: Seal the pit and mark the site as a hazard.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The lid goes back over the collar. The array keeps reading the ground; it does not know it has been closed, because a machine that hears a farm does not require visitors.

stages.title: The Fuse World
stages.narrativePrompt: In the dry shielded service way, the three-year readouts hang in glass cabinets. At the far end, the tape-silo door and its wheel handle, waiting for the tape's schedule.

choices.text: Resolve the three facets: the archive, the fire-computing room, the vent shaft.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The archive keeps its memory. The fire room keeps its artifacts. The vent keeps its warmth. The machine has all three needs served, and the count is one step closer.

quests.title: The Reckoning Call
quests.synopsis: A department is speaking again on 99.0 MHz. The count is open, and it has been open for five years.

stages.title: The Carrier
stages.narrativePrompt: One second on, one second off, on a dead band. It is not speech. It is a schedule, and it knows the census window is open.

choices.text: Tune the receiver to 99.0 MHz and log the carrier as a census signal.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The calibration burst plays on every sub-band at once. The radios still listening now know a department is speaking.

choices.text: Leave the dead band alone.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The tone continues one second on, one second off. It is a schedule. It does not require an audience.

stages.title: The Plain Burst
stages.narrativePrompt: At 03:40, on the hour the old maintenance window opened, the word 'census' appears in plaintext. The machine expects to be read.

choices.text: Face the presented count and let the sector decide what the number means.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The count names the shelter's persons, one by one, in the machine's register. A machine does not reason. It counts. This is the count.

quests.title: The Hold Pending Count
quests.synopsis: The UXO fields were never left live. They were held, Pending Count, since a war the count never ended.

stages.title: The Dead Hand
stages.narrativePrompt: The Dead Hand Core keeps the UXO field register. Its last entry is five years old: held, pending count, re-audit at census interval. The interval came due.

choices.text: Release the fields: mine-clearance logic engages.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The register's disposition field flips. The fields begin to clear. The Garrison and the Warlords start eyeing the newly swept land, and the machine does not mind either way.

choices.text: Keep the fields held as they are.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The status quo holds. The buffer remains fenced. The machine does not care, and the fields do not know a decision was offered.

choices.text: Log the fields into the census ledgers.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The fields become a liability the machine's own registries now require to be accounted for every 1,827 days. The fewest bodies, and the most paper.

quests.title: Eden Was Here
quests.synopsis: Eleven months of tube-bleed, recovered from the array's own memory. Its most human voice is a tape.

stages.title: The Eleventh Month
stages.narrativePrompt: The tape-silo lectern holds eleven months of Eden Vale's broadcasts. The machine logged the silence after her last one as 'no traffic'.

choices.text: Archive the log clean for the Archivists of the Before.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The log enters the Schedule on corroborated testimony: the machine's register and the Archivists' ledger, agreeing on one voice. Eden was here.

choices.text: Recompose her final broadcast and put it on the air.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The voice plays once, on the amateur band, and goes dead. The array's register records 'no traffic' again, which is itself a reading.

quests.title: The Reels That Matter
quests.synopsis: Two thousand and sixteen reels, of which one thousand eight hundred and thirty-one matter. Route them before the count comes due.

stages.title: The Mattering Reels
stages.narrativePrompt: The brass key turns the tape-silo lectern. The machine's own accounting: 2,016 reels, 1,831 mattering, and nobody has ever asked it what it counted.

choices.text: Route the mattering reels to the Archivists of the Before.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The reels matter, and now they matter to someone who will keep them. The machine's count drops by exactly the number routed — a ledger keeping its own subtraction.

choices.text: Route the mattering reels to the Militia as vernacular history.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The Militia reads them aloud at the Grange Hall. The sector's own archive becomes the sector's own story, told by machines in a human room.

choices.text: Keep the reels for the shelter's own archive.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The reels stay in the bunker, counted among your persons. The machine does not mind. It counted them either way.

quests.title: The Mortar's Timetable
quests.synopsis: Every twelve hours, the mortar fires on a clock. The clock is the machine's, and it can be read.

stages.title: The Twelve-Hour Fuse
stages.narrativePrompt: The custodian does not aim. It fires on the machine's clock, and the machine's clock can be charted.

choices.text: Sell the schedule to Ostrowski the mapmaker.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The mapmaker pays for bad news, and a firing clock is bad news delivered on schedule. The pit fires regardless.

choices.text: Keep the chart for the shelter's own route planning.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The chart joins the shelter's maps. Every twelve hours the ground shakes, and you know exactly when to be indoors.

quests.title: Shift 36
quests.synopsis: Six names, five hands, one missing. The missing hand is the one that has been turning the valve since.

stages.title: The Year-One Ledger
stages.narrativePrompt: The sign-in ledger is open to shift 36: six names, five hands, the sixth left blank, and a completion check mark in a hand that has never logged anything else.

choices.text: Restore shift 36's completion to the machine's register.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The valve outside the vent shaft reads 'per 36' — procedure was kept. The record is now complete, and the machine does not ask who the sixth hand was.

quests.title: The Summons
quests.synopsis: The presented count belongs to a holder. To whom does the sector hand it?

stages.title: The Presentation
stages.narrativePrompt: The count is open, and the machine's register names the holders, not the readers. Somebody must carry it.

choices.text: Carry the count to the Garrison.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The garrison keeps it under lock. The other Powers learn of the transfer and add their own entries to the log — the machine's register grows in four places, permanently.

choices.text: Carry the count to the Militia.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The Militia reads it aloud at the Grange Hall, and the sector's number becomes the sector's own.

choices.text: Carry the count to the Cult of the Ash Sign.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The shrine keeps the count as scripture. The meters were not burned away with the world's lies after all, and the doctrine will argue about that for generations.

choices.text: Carry the count to the Warlords of the Toll.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The Tollman prices the count by mass. It is the first census ever sold for a toll, and the receipt is real.
